To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The 1-particle reduced density matrix of an im-penetrable Bose gas satisfies a non-linear second order differential equation, which is the Painlevé V equation; (ii) The n-particle reduced density matrices satisfy a system of non- linear partial differential equations, which is the generalization of the Painlevé VI system to n variables.

1. the n-particle reduced density matrix of the 1-dimensional impenetrable gas of bosons satisfies the Painleve V equation (or the system of n-Painleve V equations) and 2. the 1-particles reduced density matrix satisfies the Painlev V equation.
the 1- and 2-particle density matrix of an im-penetrable Bose gas satisfy non-linear differential and partial differential equations of Painlevé type, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the quantum impenetrable 1-dimensional Bose gas.
the study of the 1-dimensional Bose gas, and the 2-dimensional quantum Ising model, as examples of integrable systems.
a class of quantum many body problems, for which we can derive non-linear differential equations of Painleve transcendent type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density matrices of the 1-dimensional Bose gas are the most complicated objects in the whole theory of Painleve equations.
the fifth Painleve transcendent describes the 2-point correlation function of an impenentrable 1-dimensional Bose gas, and the n-th Painleve transcen- dent describes the n-point function.
the density matrix of an im-penetrable Bose gas is described in terms of the fifth Painleve transcendent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2-dimensional (resp. 1-dimensional) Ising model and the 1-dimensional impenetrable gas are both related to the second (resp. fifth) Painleve transcendent.
the density matrices of the impenetrable gas are Painlevé transcendents.
the 1-dimensional gas of impenitrable Bose particles, as well as the Ising model and the Kondo problem, all are related to Painleve equations and the monodromy problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Painleve transcendents, which are the only known non-trivial solutions of non-linear ordinary differential equations with regular singular points, appear naturally in the context of quantum statistical mechanics.

, in the context of the 1D Bose gas, the Painleve equations are not only a mathematical curiosity, but they also provide a very useful and practical tool for the calculation of the density matrix of this system.
, in addition to its physical interest, the 1-dim. Bose gas provides an interesting example of the application of the monodromy-preserving deformation theory.
